microabrasion.text: Users look to microabrasion to clear white or brown spots, including fluorosis marks, so front teeth look more even in colour. The surface change is visible right after a dentist polishes the tooth, and the method has been in clinical use since the 1980s.

resin-infiltration-icon.text: Resin infiltration such as Icon is used to mask white spot lesions left by braces or early decay without drilling, so the tooth surface matches the surrounding enamel. The colour blending is visible after treatment, and many trials exist on its effect on lesion progression.

whitening-led-tray-with-red-light.text: At-home users buy LED trays with red light hoping to speed up peroxide gel whitening for a brighter smile. The gel does the bleaching; the claim that red light adds to it is a marketing premise, and trials of light in general bleaching are mixed with no red-specific data.

blue-light-teeth-whitening-device.text: Consumers use blue-light gadgets, with or without gel, to get whiter teeth at home. The idea comes from in-office light-accelerated bleaching, where some studies show light as an add-on to peroxide; light on its own has little data.

electric-toothbrush-whitening-heads.text: Users swap in whitening heads on powered brushes to lift coffee, tea and other surface stain for a brighter smile. Polishing cups and pads are designed for stain removal, though no trials of these specific heads were found.

teeth-whitening-hollywood-smile-turkey-t.text: People travel to Turkey for a veneer-and-whitening makeover that delivers a bright, uniform smile at lower prices than in Western Europe. The new look is visible once the work is fitted, and forum and clinical discussion centres on enamel removal and aftercare.

metal-braces.text: Metal braces are the standard route to straight teeth for teens and adults seeking a better smile. Alignment improves gradually over treatment, and the method is well established in orthodontics.

ceramic-braces.text: Ceramic braces are chosen by people who want straighter teeth with less visible hardware during treatment. They use the same bracket-and-wire mechanics as metal braces, so alignment follows the same established path.

direct-to-consumer-aligners-smiledirectc.text: Mail-order aligners were promoted to people wanting straighter teeth more cheaply and conveniently than traditional orthodontics. Alignment comes from the aligners moving teeth over months; SmileDirectClub, the best-known brand, went bankrupt in 2023 after professional complaints.

self-ligating-braces-damon.text: Self-ligating braces such as Damon are marketed as a faster, gentler route to straight teeth. Alignment is the established outcome; claims of speed or comfort over conventional brackets have been compared in trial reviews.

retainers.text: Retainers keep a smile straight after braces or aligners by holding teeth where they were moved. Looksmaxxing forums also debate whether retainers affect palate or jaw development, a theory that has not been tested.

fixed-lingual-retainer.text: A bonded wire behind the lower front teeth is used to preserve the alignment gained from braces without a removable appliance to remember. It is an established orthodontic retention method, especially where relapse is considered likely.

chain: Vibration, light or surgery stimulates bone
accelerated-orthodontics-acceledent-prop.text: People in braces or aligners look at AcceleDent, light therapy and Propel micro-perforations to shorten treatment time and reach a straight smile sooner. Evidence for the non-surgical options is described as weak, while surgical versions have shown more effect.

surgically-assisted-rapid-palatal-expans.text: Adults who want a wider upper jaw use SARPE after non-surgical expansion is no longer an option, and forum posters link the widening to a fuller, better-proportioned face. The skeletal widening is established for narrow-jaw bite problems, while the facial-aesthetic benefit is mostly anecdotal.

marpe-mini-implant-palate-expander.text: Teens and young adults use MARPE to widen the upper jaw without cutting bone, and forum users hope for a broader midface and cheekbone support. Studies show skeletal widening for narrow jaws; cosmetic facial effects are barely studied.

palate-expander.text: Palate expanders are used mainly in children and teens to widen a narrow upper jaw, and looksmaxxing posters hope for a wider, better-looking face as well. Widening for crossbite and narrow palates is well established; effects on facial looks are largely unstudied.

orthotropics.text: Followers of John Mew's orthotropics, the root of mewing, hold that tongue posture and oral habits shape the jaw and midface during growth, and adopt it for a more defined face. Mainstream orthodontics regards the evidence for that facial effect as inadequate.

facial-growth-guidance-appliances-bioblo.text: Parents and orthotropics followers use growth guidance appliances in children to steer jaw development toward a better-balanced face. Twin Block is a mainstream functional appliance, while Biobloc belongs to the orthotropics camp, and evidence for its facial effects is limited.

bimax-double-jaw-surgery.text: Bimax surgery is the forum term for orthognathic surgery that moves both jaws, sought for a more defined profile and a corrected bite. The facial change is visible after healing, and the procedure has documented functional benefits.

genioplasty.text: Genioplasty moves or reshapes the chin bone, or adds an implant, to improve chin projection and lower-face balance. The shape change is immediately visible, and forum posters discuss it as an alternative to double-jaw surgery.

gummy-smile-botox.text: Botulinum toxin in the upper lip muscles is used by people who want less gum showing when they smile. The lowered lip line is visible within days and temporary, and many small trials have measured it.

crown-lengthening-gingivectomy.text: Crown lengthening and gingivectomy reshape the gum line so teeth look longer and less gum shows, used for gummy smiles where the gum line is the cause. The change in tooth display is visible once healed.

lip-repositioning-surgery.text: Lip repositioning is used for gummy smiles caused by a hypermobile upper lip, limiting how far the lip rises on smiling. The reduced gum display is visible after healing.

gum-contouring-laser.text: Laser gum contouring is used to even out the gum line and show more tooth, as a laser version of gingivectomy. The reshaped gum line is visible after healing, with little direct study of the laser itself.

enamel-reshaping-contouring.text: Enamel reshaping is used for quick, subtle fixes to uneven edges, chips and slightly long or pointed teeth, mostly on front teeth. The change is visible straight away.

dental-implants.text: Dental implants are used to replace missing teeth with a fixed, natural-looking result. Forum posters also speculate about thickening the jaw or building up a recessed chin with implants and grafts; that jaw-reshaping use is not shown in studies.

crowns-and-bridges.text: Crowns restore damaged teeth and bridges fill gaps from missing teeth, so the smile looks complete and uniform. The restored look is visible once fitted, and the methods are long established.

smile-makeover-digital-smile-design.text: A smile makeover bundles whitening, bonding, veneers, crowns, gum contouring and orthodontics into one planned redesign, often previewed with digital smile design. The new smile is visible once the work is complete.

chain: More attractive smile in person and photos
smile-training-smile-mirror-practice.text: People practise smiling in a mirror or on camera to find a more natural, flattering expression for daily life and photos. It is free to try, and no trials of the practice itself were located.

smile-maxxing.text: Smile maxxing is a community umbrella term for improving the smile through whitening, alignment, cosmetic dentistry, gum and lip work, or better expression. It has no formal definition, and no published research uses the term.
